welcome.label: Welcome · Proof for the Steel Bin

parts.label: ♻️ The steel bin
parts.title: The haul is at the recycling center
parts.body: Eight things from the pond cleanup.

parts.label: 📞 Dana’s voicemail
parts.title: She wants proof
parts.body: Not “it looks like steel.” Real proof.

parts.label: 🔍 The question
parts.title: Which go in the steel bin?
parts.body: And what proof do we send?

welcome.script:
(Hold up a spoon and a fork.) Both look like steel. Will a magnet grab both? Hmm. You can’t tell by looking.

[ON SCREEN: The steel bin]
Our pond haul is at the recycling center, and only magnetic steel goes in the steel bin.

[ON SCREEN: Dana’s voicemail]
Dana won’t fill the bin on a guess. She wants proof.

[ON SCREEN: The question]
Which things go in, and what proof do we send? Play Dana’s voicemail just below me.

warmup.label: Warm-Up · spot the differences (Clue 1)

parts.label: ⚖️ Fair?
parts.title: Whose result do we trust?
parts.body: Find every place they tested differently.

warmup.script:
(Hold a fridge magnet very close to a paperclip, then very far away.) Close… it jumps. Far… nothing. Same paperclip!

[ON SCREEN: Two pages]
Kai and Mo tested the same bottle cap and got opposite results. Tap every place where they tested differently.

[ON SCREEN: Fair?]
Then decide whose result to trust. Answer the question, and Clue one is yours.

part1.label: Part 1 · the how-sure dial (Clue 2)

parts.label: ⭐ Gold star
parts.title: Sure and wrong = big learning
parts.body: A surprise is how scientists learn.

part1.script:
(Hold up a can of beans.) We call this a tin can. Will a magnet stick to tin? Make a prediction… how sure are you?

[ON SCREEN: Predict]
Predict, turn the dial to show how sure you are, then press Test it.

[ON SCREEN: Gold star]
If you were sure and wrong, you earn a gold star. Wrong predictions are where scientists learn the most!

part2.label: Part 2 · messy notes to a data table (Clue 3)

parts.label: 📝 Sticky notes
parts.title: Mo’s messy notes
parts.body: Which thing is each note about?

part2.script:
(Wave a handful of sticky notes, or scraps of paper, and drop them.) Oops. Which one was which?

[ON SCREEN: Sticky notes]
Mo wrote every result on a sticky note. Read each one and drag it onto the right row of the data table.

[ON SCREEN: A data table]
Rows and columns keep every result in its place. Watch the spoon row. There’s a surprise hiding there!

part3.label: Part 3 · make it a fair test
part3.script:
(Hold up one finger.) One. A fair test changes only ONE thing.

[ON SCREEN: Fair test]
Same magnet, same distance, same way of moving it. Only the material changes. Then the results really mean something.

explore.label: Part 4 · slide to the jump (Clue 4)
explore.script:
(Slowly slide a paperclip toward a magnet on your desk until it jumps.) There! It jumped!

[ON SCREEN: Lock it]
In Part 4, lock the fair-test settings first: the same magnet, and every item starts at 10 centimeters.

[ON SCREEN: Slide]
Then slide each item toward the magnet. Does it jump? Where? Your data table fills in. That’s Clue four.

assignment.label: Assignment · crack the case

parts.label: 🔓 Crack the case
parts.title: What goes in the steel bin?
parts.body: Use all four clues. And remember Dana wants proof.

assignment.script:
[ON SCREEN: Crack the case]
Use all four clues to fill Dana’s steel bin, and choose the proof to send. Then look for a real giant magnet!

[ON SCREEN: Your case report]
Next, two short answers. For Part C, test six things at home the fair way, then sketch and label your two sorting circles. Last comes your CER.

evidence.label: Use your evidence · CER

parts.label: 💬 The claim
parts.title: A classmate says…
parts.body: “You don’t need to write down test results. Just remember them.”

parts.label: 🧩 The planner
parts.title: Claim · Evidence · Reasoning
rows: Tap I agree or I disagree.

evidence.script:
(Tap your head.) I’ll just remember it all… what was row six again?

[ON SCREEN: The claim]
A classmate says you don’t need to write results down. Think about Kai and Mo, Mo’s sticky notes, and Dana.

[ON SCREEN: The planner]
Tap your side and two facts. Then explain how they prove your claim. Try starting with “This shows that…”

closing.label: Case closed

parts.label: 🧾 Your specimen
parts.title: Dana’s steel-bin receipt
parts.body: Finish the checklist to stamp CASE CLOSED.

parts.label: ➡ Next week
parts.title: Mystery materials
parts.body: And what happens when matter changes.

closing.script:
(Pretend to stamp a receipt.) Received! The steel bin is full.

[ON SCREEN: Your specimen]
Finish your checklist, and Dana’s receipt goes into your Field Notebook.

[ON SCREEN: A giant magnet]
Did you see the steel mill’s giant lifting magnet? It sorts steel just like you did.

[ON SCREEN: Confetti]

[ON SCREEN: Next week]
Next week: mystery materials!

quiz.label: Self-Check
quiz.script: Quick check: three questions, one at a time. It’s not graded. If you miss one, read the hint and try again.
